newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal premier to quit as government loses vote.
newsitem.headline: Nepal premier to quit as government loses vote.

text.p: Nepal's Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba said on Thursday he would resign after his 17-month-old centre-right coalition lost a crucial parliamentary vote of confidence.

"I accept the verdict gracefully and I will resign," Deuba told Reuters after the vote. Asked when he will resign, he said: "I will have to check whether to personally go to the King (Birendra) or if I can send my resignation," he said.

Deuba's government received 101 votes against a required minimum of 103 during voting on the motion, which he himself had moved to demonstrate the coalition's majority in the 205-seat lower house of parliament.
Lawmakers said two of Deuba's Nepali Congress party lawmakers were not present for the voting on Thursday. This could not be officially confirmed.
The lawmakers said the Nepali Congress was holding a meeting of its deputies at Deuba's official residence. The Congress could try to form a new government under a new party leader, they said.
The alternative would be for the opposition United Marxist Leninist (UML) party to attempt to form a new government.
The communist UML had formed a minority government after elections in November 1994 threw up a fragmented parliament.
But it was defeated in September 1995, when Deuba assumed power by cobbling together a three-party coalition with crucial support from the Rashtriya Prajatantra Party (RPP).

Madhav Kumar Nepal, general secretary of the UML, said his party's standing committee was scheduled to meet later on Thursday. "We will discuss the possibility of a new government with other major parties," he said. He gave no details.
Ninety-two MPs voted against the motion, but the higher number of votes won by Deuba was not enough as the constitution requires the government to prove a majority in the total strength of the house.
"Since the vote is inadequate the confidence motion has been rejected," said Ram Chandra Poudel, speaker of the House of Representatives, after announcing the results of the vote.
The next parliamentary elections are officially not due until 1999.
The Nepali Congress party, which has 87 seats, lost its majority last December following a split in the ranks of the RPP, which had 19 seats. The UML controls 94 votes.
Deuba had then lost a censure motion, but did not resign. He promised to hold a fresh confidence vote, which he held and lost on Thursday.
Nepal launched multi-party democracy under a constitutional monarchy in 1990 at the end of a bloody pro-democracy movement.

The Nepali Congress won power in the first general elections that year, but its government fell prematurely after a split in the party which was reduced to a minority. The second general elections in 1994 returned a hung parliament.
